reading.body:
Google does not publish megawatt capacity or square footage for individual buildings at this Fairfield County site, which is part of a larger New Albany/Columbus-area campus spanning Franklin, Licking, and Fairfield counties. The operator's disclosure policy is to report investment figures only at the state aggregate level. This means the facility's power demand and rack count cannot be determined from published sources.

The New Albany/Columbus corridor now hosts Google, AWS, and Meta as major hyperscale investors simultaneously, with Google's combined state commitment reported at $1.7 billion across new campuses in this region and Lancaster. Ohio ranks ninth among states in this registry by published data center capacity, with 60.4 MW disclosed across eight facilities out of 76 mapped statewide, indicating most of the state's infrastructure operates without public specification.

Whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends on capacity not published here. The regional concentration of three hyperscale operators in the same corridor suggests the area may become a significant cluster, but without per-facility power figures, this site cannot yet measure its contribution to the grid constraint on AI.
